exchanges: Hi. I just finished my first full week at McGill and I am exhausted.
That is a big milestone. What has been the hardest part so far?
Honestly, the reading load. Linguistics has way more reading than I expected.
Intro courses often front-load the reading. It usually gets easier once you find a rhythm.
My roommate Ines has been great, though. She cooked for the whole floor on Wednesday.
That is a generous way to start the year.
She made pierogi from her grandmother's recipe. She says it's her favourite thing in the world to eat.
Homemade ones are a lot of work, so the floor was lucky.
I also met someone named Oluwaseun at orientation. We ended up watching the basketball game together at a pub.
Sounds like a good way to make a friend.
He is obsessed with the Raptors. He was shouting at the screen the whole time.
Some fans take every game personally.
My sister Leila called last night. She's due in November, so I'm already planning to fly home.
That is exciting news. Will it be her first?
Yes, her first. The whole family is beside themselves.
First babies tend to have that effect on a family.
Unfortunately the family news isn't all good. My uncle Farid has gout again and can barely walk.
I am sorry to hear that. Flare-ups can be very painful.
He's stubborn about his diet, so it keeps coming back.
That is a common pattern, unfortunately.
And my great-uncle Karim, who is ninety, just got over shingles. He's tougher than all of us.
That is an impressive recovery at his age.
Our TA for syntax, Bjorn, is very strict about citations.
Strict TAs can be a pain, but it pays off later.
He grew up in Bergen and keeps comparing the rain here to home.
He probably finds the weather here mild by comparison.
Speaking of things I forget, I have a checkup at the campus clinic on Friday.
Put a reminder in your phone so it does not slip by.
Good idea. I've already missed one tutorial this week by forgetting.
It happens in the first weeks. Most instructors post their slides.
Correction about my sister, by the way. I misremembered. Leila's due in December, not November.
Thanks for clarifying. That puts it right around the holidays.
Exactly. Hopefully the flights are not too expensive then.
Booking early usually helps.
Next year I want to get out of residence. I'm thinking of moving to an apartment in the Plateau.
That is a popular area for students, with lots of cafes.
Rent is high, but it would be worth it to have a real kitchen.
A kitchen would make a big difference for both budget and meals.
Sorry, what did my great-uncle come down with? I'm writing him a card.
Thanks. I'll mail it tomorrow.
He will probably love getting real mail.
I bought a ukulele this afternoon at a pawn shop. I've wanted to learn to play for years.
That is a fun instrument to start on, and it is easy to carry around.

earlier_question.right_reply: Your great-uncle Karim was getting over shingles.
earlier_question.wrong_reply: Your great-uncle Karim was getting over gout.

questions.message: What food does Ines like best?
Leila's baby is coming in December, right?
Which instrument did I just get?
I think I'll make some tea and go to bed early tonight.
Do you know what Bjorn's favourite food is?
What team does my uncle Farid cheer for?
Sorry, remind me what illness Karim had?
